indexableObject.name: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971
Purpose
•	To legally regulate the termination of pregnancies under specified conditions and by registered medical practitioners.
Key Provisions
1.	Gestational Limits for Termination: - Up to 20 weeks: Requires the opinion of one registered medical practitioner.
•	20-24 weeks: Needs the opinion of two registered medical practitioners, limited to prescribed categories of women.
•	Beyond 24 weeks: Only permissible if substantial foetal abnormalities are confirmed by a constituted Medical Board.
2.	Medical Board: - Established by each State/Union Territory.
•	Comprises specialists (Gynaecologist, Paediatrician, Radiologist/Sonologist, etc.).
•	Mandated to diagnose substantial foetal abnormalities for late-term terminations.
3.	Authorized Facilities: - Government hospitals.
•	Places approved by the Government or a District Level Committee.
4.	Consent Requirements: - Minors/Mentally Ill: Written consent from a guardian.
•	Others: Consent of the pregnant woman.
5.	Confidentiality: - Practitioners must maintain patient confidentiality.
•	Breach punishable by up to 1 year imprisonment, fine, or both.
6.	Legal Safeguards: - Good Faith Protection: Immunity for actions taken in good faith.
•	Penalties for Illegal Terminations: 2-7 years imprisonment for unauthorized practitioners or unapproved locations.
7.	Administrative Framework: - Central Government: Empowered to make rules.
•	State Governments: Authority to make regulations and form Medical Boards.
Important Provisions
•	Section 3: Outlines conditions for legal termination.
•	Section 4: Specifies approved locations for the procedure.
•	Section 5A: Ensures patient privacy.
•	Section 8: Protects good faith actions.

indexableObject.name: Definitions

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
In this Act
(a) "agricultural development" means any work undertaken for the development of any agricultural land or for raising agricultural production, and includes drainage, ground-water development and soil conservation;
(b) "agricultural production" includes production of agriculture, horticulture, pisciculture, forestry, sericulture bee-keeping, dairy farming piggery and poultry farming and also includes such other types of production as are notified by the State Government as ancillary or incidental there to;
(c) "authority" means an Area Development Authority established under section 3;
(d) "chairman" means the Chairman of the Authority;
(e) "command" area in relation to an irrigation project, means an area which for purpose of, irrigation can be commanded through the irrigation project and the limits of which are notified by the State Government;
(f) "cost of works" means all costs, charges and expenses as estimated by the Authority, and which the Authority may have to incur on, or in connection with, execution of the works, and includes, any other charges or fees as may be prescribed; and also includes all expenses which, may be incurred by the Authority in recovery thereof;
(g) "district committee" means the District Committee established under section 18;
(h) "ineligible person" means a person not eligible for ordinary land development loans and belonging to any of the following categories-
(i) farmer without any valid title;
(ii) illegal occupant;
(iii) minor;
(iv) land holder unable to get institutional finance because of heavy
indebtedness to institutional sources which are to cleared before obtaining finance for further capital investment;
(v) Rural artisan; or
(vi) Agricultural labourers ;
(i) "land development" means any of the following works, namely :-
(i) Construction, renovation, redesigning, realigning and lining of water courses;
(ii) Land leveling and land shaping, including, realignment of field boundaries;
(iii) Digging of drop structures, culverts and farm roads in the fields;
(iv) Providing of drop structures, culverts, and farm roads in the fields;
(v) Land reclamation by use of engineering, biological and chemical measures, including leaching;
(vi) Contour bunding and nala bunding;
(vii) Growing of trees, plants, shrubs and grasses;
(viii) Development of permanent and temporary pastures, farm forestry and commercial afforestation.
(ix) Such other works as may be necessary or incidental to development of land or ground or flow water potential and for optimizing the utilization of land and water resources; and
(x) Repairing and maintenance of any of the foregoing works;
(j) "land holder" means a person in actual possession of the land, whether as a owner or a tenant or sub-tenant or as mortgagee in possession or licensee or otherwise, and includes person who is likely to be benefited by land development and the expression land holding shall be construed accordingly;
(k) "ordinary loan" means a loan granted by a bank or any financing institution to a land holder against mortgage of land or any other security;.
(l) "outlet command" means an area served for irrigation purposes by a particular outlet as specified by the Authority;
(m) "plan" means a plan prepared by the Authority under section 14;
(n) "project" means a project of or scheme of land development;
(o) "project administration" means an officer appointed as such by the State Government by notification;
(p) "project director" means such officer as may be nominated by the Authority and shall also include such other officer or officers as may be authorized by the authority to exercise the powers and discharge the duties of a Project Director;
(q) "Proportionate cost of works" means cost of work recoverable from a land holder in proportion to the extent of works to be done on or for the benefit of his land holding.
(r) "record of rights" has the same meaning as in the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901;
(s) "Secretary" means Secretary of the Authority;
(t) "small farmer", marginal farmer, 'agricultural. labourer' and village artisans means persons defined as such by notification by the State Government from time to time;
(u) "special loan" means a loan granted by the Authority to an ineligible person;
(v) "works" includes any work relating to land development to be executed under a project under this Act.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) The Government shall constitute in every district a District Planning Committee to consolidate the plans prepared by the Zilla Parishad, Gram Panchayats, Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.
(2) The District Planning Committee shall consist of--
(a) members of the House of the People who represent the whole or part of the district;
(b) all the members or the State Legislative Assembly whose constituencies lie within the district;
(c) Adhyaksha of the Zilla Parishad;
(d) Mayor or the President of the Municipal Corporation or the Municipal Council respectively, having jurisdiction over the headquarters of the district; and
(e) such number of persons not less than four-fifth of the total number of members of the Committee as may be specified by the Government elected in the prescribed manner from amongst the members of the Zilla Parishad, Nagar Panchayat and Councillors of the Municipal Corporation and the Municipal Councils in the district, in proportion to the ratio between the population of the rural areas and of the urban areas in the district.
(3) The Chairman of the District Co-operative Banks and of the Land Development Bank shall be permanent invitees of the Committee.

Self assessment and submission of return.--(1) After the coming into force of the Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2003, any owner of any vacant land or covered space of building or any other person liable to pay the property tax or any occupier in the absence of such owner or person, shall file a return of self assessment within sixty days of the coming into force of the aforesaid Act.

(a) any new building or existing building which has not been assessed; or
(b) any existing building which has been redeveloped or substantially altered or improved after the last assessment, but has not been subjected to revision of assessment consequent upon such redevelopment or alteration or improvement) as the case may be.
(5) Such owner or person, as the case may be, shall furnish to the Commissioner a return of selfassessment in such form, and in such manner, as may be specified in the bye-laws and every such return shall be accompanied by proof of payment of property tax and interest, if any.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980
Purpose: An Act to provide for the conservation of forests and for matters connected therewith or ancillary or incidental thereto, with a focus on achieving national targets of Net Zero Emission by 2070, enhancing forest carbon stocks, and increasing forest and tree cover.
Key Provisions:
1.	Short Title, Extent, and Commencement:
•	Title: The Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
•	Extent: Whole of India.
•	Commencement: Deemed to have come into force on 25th October, 1980.
2.	Specific Provisions: - 1A. Act to Cover Certain Land:
•	Covers land declared/ notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, or other laws.
•	Includes land recorded as forest in Government records from 25th October, 1980, with exceptions for land changed to non-forest use before 12th December, 1996.
•	Exemptions for specific small areas alongside rail lines or public roads for habitation or roadside amenity.
•	Other Sections (Overview):
•	2: Restriction on dereservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purposes.
•	2A: Appeal process to the National Green Tribunal.
•	3: Establishment of an Advisory Committee.
•	3A-3C: Penalties, offences by authorities, and Central Government's directive powers.
•	4 & 5: Rule-making power and repeal with savings clause.
Preamble Highlights:
•	Achieving Net Zero Emission by 2070.
•	Creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3.0 billion tons of CO₂ equivalent by 2030.
•	Increasing forest and tree cover to one-third of India's land area.
•	Preserving biodiversity and enhancing economic, social, and environmental benefits for forest-dependent communities.

(2) Where any creditor violates the provisions of section 14, any person who knowingly and wilfully authorised or permitted such contravention by a creditor shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year, but may extend to five years, or with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but may extend to one crore rupees, or with both.
